sections.html:
Ridley Township is a compact, mostly built-out suburb in southeastern Delaware County where owners are long-settled and the housing stock is older. A sale here comes down to a short call to the township's Code Enforcement office, the county's 1% local transfer tax default, and a buyer pool that is mostly local.

The township includes Folsom, Woodlyn, Crum Lynne and Holmes, plus parts of Morton and Secane. Rutledge Borough sits entirely inside Ridley's boundaries, and Ridley Park Borough is surrounded on three sides by the township, so the municipal line is not always obvious from a street address. Check which municipality your deed names before you file anything.

A 93.3% same-house rate means most owners stay put, so houses that do come up often belong to long-term owners, estates or retirees. If you have owned the house for decades, get a repair estimate before you pick a price.

sections.h2: Code Enforcement and what the township requires
sections.html:
Phone the township Code Enforcement office at 610-534-4803 well ahead of settlement. Sellers are expected to contact it for the details that apply to their address.

Owners of rental units must hold an annual certificate of use for each dwelling unit, whether occupied or empty. If you are selling a duplex or a house that was rented, confirm that the certificate is current so it does not become a closing problem.

  • Ask what inspections or forms apply to a sale at your address.
  • Ask whether any open violations, stormwater issues or unpermitted work are on file.
  • Ask for the current fee list, since permit and certificate charges are set locally.
  • Keep sidewalks and shared driveways clear of snow and ice within 24 hours after snow stops. The township enforces that rule, and buyers walking a property in winter will notice.

The township also keeps a code book, a zoning map and a stormwater management ordinance, which matter if a buyer plans an addition or paving.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Ridley sale
sections.html:
Expect the county default here: 1% goes to the state and 1% to the township. Ridley is not on the Recorder of Deeds list of places charging a higher local rate. Ring the Recorder to confirm the combined 2% before you lock in your closing figures.

State rules make buyer and seller jointly liable. Some transfers are exempt, among them certain family transfers and property passing through an estate. Even so, put who pays in the contract.

  • The Recorder of Deeds is in Room 108 of the Government Center at 201 West Front Street in Media, phone 610-891-4152.
  • Recording hours are 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., a full hour before the 4:30 p.m. office close.
  • Ask your closing agent how the recording fee and the two taxes are paid, because the office takes them separately.
  • A deed that leaves off the full price needs the Statement of Value (REV-183) attached.

Deeds for many municipalities are filed in the same office, so make sure yours names Ridley Township. A mistake there changes the local tax line.

Three bills reach a Ridley homeowner: Delaware County, Ridley Township and the Ridley School District. Call the Delaware County Assessment Office for the current appeal deadline and form, and ask the township treasurer for the tax certification before closing.

Delaware County's countywide reassessment took effect in January 2021, so values across the county were reset to the same base year. If you think your assessed value is too high you can appeal, though the bill stays due while the appeal is pending.

Stormwater is its own cost. The township's stormwater management ordinance was last updated in September 2022, and a stormwater fee schedule sits on its code page. Ask how the fee is billed on your parcel and whether any credit applies.

Students living in the township generally attend the Ridley School District, and Our Lady of Angels Regional School is the nearby Catholic option. Families often filter searches by district, so put the school assignment near the top of a listing. Parts of Morton and Secane lie inside the township, so check the school district on your tax bill.

Highway access helps resale. Interstate 95 crosses the southern part of the township, U.S. 13 follows Chester Pike, and SEPTA bus routes 37, 113 and 114 serve the area.

List the house if it is updated and you can price it against recent sales nearby. Lean toward cash if the house is dated, an estate is involved, or you must move by a set date.

  • For an estate sale, confirm who has legal authority to sign the deed before listing.
  • For a tenant-occupied house, confirm the annual certificate of use and the lease terms.
  • For a quick sale, ask the buyer to put the closing date and who pays transfer tax in writing.

Whatever route you pick, gather the tax bills, the deed and any township notices before you call anyone. With 73.7% of Ridley homes owner-occupied and few households moving in a given year, a clean file and a firm closing date set one offer apart from another.

1. Call Code Enforcement at 610-534-4803 and ask what your address needs before settlement.
  2. Confirm the rental certificate of use is current if anyone has lived in the house as a tenant.
  3. Clear snow and ice from sidewalks and shared driveways, and settle any open violation or unpermitted work item the township has on file.
  4. Request the tax certification from the township treasurer, and ask the county about the current appeal deadline if you plan to contest the assessment.
  5. Have the closing agent record the deed at the Recorder of Deeds in Media, with the recording fee, the state tax and the local tax paid separately.

A cash buyer shortens the financing portion of this list, but the township and recording steps stay. Plan them around the office hours above, since recording ends at 3:30 p.m. and a late-day closing can push the filing to the next business day. Ask your closing agent which day the deed will actually reach the office.

faqs.q: Does Ridley Township require an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: Call the Code Enforcement office at 610-534-4803 to find out. Sellers are told to contact that office for the necessary information before settlement, so the answer for your address comes from them.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax rate in Ridley Township?
faqs.a: The county default of 1% state and 1% local applies, and Ridley is not among Delaware County's higher-rate exceptions. Confirm the figure with the Recorder of Deeds before you finalize your closing numbers.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Ridley rental property with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. The township requires an annual certificate of use for each rental dwelling unit, occupied or not, so keep that current. Review the lease for how the buyer takes over the tenancy.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Ridley Township?
faqs.a: Students living in the township generally attend the Ridley School District. Parts of Morton and Secane lie inside the township, so check the school district on your tax bill.

faqs.q: Where is the Delaware County Recorder of Deeds?
faqs.a: In Room 108 of the Government Center, 201 West Front Street, Media. Recording hours run 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., and the office phone is 610-891-4152.
